item.title: Steelers vs. Saints score, live updates: Aaron Rodgers, Pittsburgh face New Orleans in NFL's first regular-season game in Paris
item.description: The Steelers and Saints will play in the league's first-ever regular-season game in Paris.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will face off in the league's first-ever regular-season game in Paris on Sunday, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET at the Stade de France.

The Steelers (4-2) are riding high after a 13-point fourth-quarter comeback win in overtime over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Aaron Rodgers continues to build on his connection with second-round rookie wideout Germie Bernard, who had 11 catches for 87 yards and a score in Week 6. Running back Jaylen Warren has also been a steady force, averaging 5.5 yards per carry and a career-best 119.7 scrimmage yards per game.

The Saints (2-4) snapped a three-game losing streak in Week 6 with a 34-27 win over the New York Giants. Quarterback Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and added another on the ground, currently fantasy football's overall QB5 on the year. Despite their slow start to the season, the Saints remain just one game back of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints head to France in Week 7, airing on NFL Network.

Matt’s (LaFleur) is doing a hell of a job. They’ve gotten better every week. They settled some things in that o-line. (Jonathan) Ganon’s doing a hell of a job with that defense, too. They’ve just steadily gotten better and better, and they’re playing at a very high level right now. Offensively, (Jordan) Love, man. He makes it go. He’s the secret sauce, and (Christian) Watson and (Matthew) Golden, they’re dangerous threats down the field, and he’s going to give them opportunities that shows up every week. (Tucker) Kraft has come off the injury nicely. He’s gotten better every week. He’s playing good football right now. This team’s playing at a high level. They’re big, physical and special teams. They play hard. This will be an outstanding test for us. Hell of an opponent. First division game of the season at home. item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Lineup advice for Week 7 from Justin Boone
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone reveals his lineup advice for Week 7.
item.content:encoded:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 7 rankings.

Starts

Jordan Love, QB, Packers

at Lions

Love has finished as a fantasy QB1 three times already this season, including each of his past two outings. 

Next up is a divisional date with a Detroit defense allowing the most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Every passer who has faced the Lions this season has ended that week as a top-seven fantasy starter. 

Love also had a huge game in his last trip to Detroit, throwing for four touchdowns and scoring the second-most fantasy points among QBs in Week 13 last season. 

Other QBs to start:

  • C.J. Stroud vs. Giants – With the Texans embracing a more pass-heavy approach, Stroud has been a top-five fantasy QB in two of his last three appearances. Hosting a Giants defense that's the seventh easiest matchup for fantasy QBs should result in another strong start. 

  • Kyler Murray vs. Colts – Injuries to Murray and Justin Jefferson have prevented the duo from suiting up at the same time for most of the season. Fortunately, they finally played a full game together in Week 5 and unsurprisingly it was Murray's best performance as a Viking. Coming off the bye, they'll take on a struggling Colts team that permits the 11th-most points to fantasy QBs and is on the verge of a fire sale.

Woody Marks, RB, Texans

vs. Giants

During his first season and a half in the league, Marks has been an adequate but unspectacular starter when called upon. Spike-weeks are rare for the sophomore, who started in the second half of his rookie campaign and has been back in the lead role with David Montgomery sidelined the last couple of weeks. 

However, the coaching staff has consistently praised Marks for his improvement from Year 1 to Year 2 and we have seen him top 80 scrimmage yards each of the past two games — while handling over 77% of the snaps in both contests. The only thing holding him back is a lack of touchdowns, but he found the end zone in the two prior outings. Now, we just need him to put it all together. 

The Giants game is setting up to be that spot for Marks. Montgomery is out again and last week's backup, Jawhar Jordan, has been placed on injured reserve, positioning Marks for a sizable workload. 

New York's defense is also one to target. The G-Men have allowed three top-12 RB finishes, as well as double-digit fantasy days to six different ball carriers already. With Houston projected as 10.5-point favorites at home, Marks should have a positive game script and all the volume he can handle.

Other RBs to start:

  • Ollie Gordon II at Jets – Gordon was impressive in his last three outings before the bye, posting 56 yards, 100 yards and 88 yards, respectively, while scoring a touchdown in each game. That also occurred against three tougher run defenses (Chiefs, Vikings, Bengals). The Jets are the 11th-most generous defense for fantasy RBs, making this his easiest matchup since taking over as starter. 

  • J.K. Dobbins at Cardinals – With four teams on bye and a variety of injuries, Dobbins is getting pushed up the rankings a bit this week. However, the veteran has also been given at least 18 touches in three of his last four games and scored a TD in consecutive weeks. The Broncos are favored by 4.5 points on the road against an Arizona defense that just let both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum finish as top-24 fantasy RBs against them last week. 

  • Jordan Mason vs. Colts – The Vikings have leaned on the run more this season and Aaron Jones Sr. has had to shoulder most of that volume with Mason on IR. However, before getting hurt, it was Mason who led the team in carries (15) and rushing yards (59) while also scoring a touchdown in Week 1. Coming off the bye and facing a floundering Colts squad, Minnesota should control this game. Don't be shocked if Mason earns more touches than Jones, after the 31-year-old's busy month — which included playing through an MCL sprain. 

Jameson Williams, WR, Lions

vs. Packers

Williams is a boom-or-bust fantasy WR3 who was heating up before the bye thanks to a six-catch, 102-yard effort in Week 4 and a 47-yard, two-touchdown outing in Week 5. 

Now, the Lions return to the field at home to face the Packers, in a game with the highest projected point total on the week (53.5). 

In his last two home games against Green Bay, Williams has delivered stat lines of 5-80-0 (2024) and 7-144-1 (2025). I'm expecting another solid performance in this likely shootout. 

Other WRs to start:

  • Germie Bernard vs. Saints (Paris) – Bernard has earned 21 targets over the past two games, while becoming one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite pass-catchers. When a rookie is playing over 90% of the snaps and producing like this with back-to-back weeks with at least 80 yards, you don't put them on your bench. Bernard is a top-24 fantasy wideout for Week 7. 

  • Jalen Coker vs. Buccaneers – Coker is taking his game to another level this season with at least nine targets in each of his three healthy appearances, leading to top-24 fantasy WR results every time. In the past two weeks, the Bucs defense has let two receivers reach double-digit fantasy points in both games. Coker and Tetairoa McMillan will continue that trend. 

  • Carnell Tate vs. Browns – Tate isn't getting the hype he deserves because the Titans are an uninspiring franchise at the moment. However, the rookie is on the verge of becoming a must-start in fantasy with stat lines of 6-58-0, 9-145-0 and 6-70-1 in three of his last four contests. 

Tyler Higbee, TE, Rams

at Raiders

Higbee was going to be my recommended start even before Puka Nacua popped up with a calf injury on Thursday. While there’s optimism the Rams' star wideout will be able to play, Higbee is still a strong option since Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson are already sidelined. 

Despite a quieter outing in Week 6, Higbee was on a roll in the previous three contests with 62 yards and a TD in Week 3 (TE7), 67 yards in Week 4 (TE14) and 83 yards in Week 5 (TE10).

Meanwhile, his next opponent, the Raiders, are giving up the seventh most fantasy points to tight ends. If Puka plays, Higbee will be a top-10 option. But if Puka is ruled out, Higbee has top-five upside. 

Other TEs to start:

  • T.J. Hockenson vs. Colts – We're finally going to see the Vikings offense with most of its starters on the field this week. That's bad news for the Colts defense. Indy is a plus matchup for tight ends and has allowed big days to the likes of Travis Kelce and Pat Freiermuth. Hockenson should be a solid streamer this week. 

  • Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. 49ers – Pitts has shown signs of life for three straight weeks with 47 yards, 42 yards and a touchdown and most recently, 60 yards and two TDs, respectively. The matchup with San Francisco isn't good, but we just watched Chig Okonkwo post 7-69-0 on them Monday night. Pitts is in play once again as a low-end TE1 in a game with a healthy 50.5 projected point total. 

Sits

Patrick Mahomes, QB, Chiefs

at Seahawks

After starting the season with two straight top-10 fantasy results, Mahomes hasn't cracked the QB1 range in his last three games (QB20, QB13, QB23). 

Injuries to his receiving corps and offensive line have been a problem and could be exposed even more when he travels to Seattle. The Seahawks defense allows the fewest passing yards and the second fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks. 

It's also worth noting, Mahomes isn't running as much coming off the ACL last season, as was expected coming into the year. After averaging over 30 rushing yards per contest in 2025, he's down to 11 yards per game this year. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Tyler Shough vs. Steelers (Paris) – Shough is a risky player to put in the sit column, given the Saints' uptempo style and tendency to find themselves in shootouts. However, the Steelers are allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks and have only let one QB top 14 points against them this year. 

  • Sam Darnold vs. Chiefs – Darnold has only finished inside the top-15 fantasy QBs once this season and now faces a Chiefs defense that's the third-toughest matchup for his position. 

Emanuel Wilson, RB, Seahawks

vs. Chiefs

Fantasy managers had the rug pulled out from under them on Friday afternoon when the Seahawks announced that Zach Charbonnet would not be making his season debut in Week 7. That means we'll get another week with the combination of Wilson and George Holani.

Even though Wilson has had some strong performances in his relief starts this year, this isn't a time to get him in your lineup. The Chiefs defense has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards, fourth-fewest rushing TDs and sixth-fewest fantasy points to running backs. 

If you do start Wilson out of desperation, you'll need him to find the end zone in order to pay off for fantasy. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Alvin Kamara vs. Steelers (Paris) – Kamara is clearly a declining player, but his veteran savvy has helped him find the end zone and produce as a flex option a couple of times in the last month. In Week 6, Kendre Miller handled the bulk of the early-down work and C.J. Donaldson continued to be involved as a pass-catching option. So, expecting fluky long touchdowns from Kamara is a dangerous path to take. 

  • Cam Skattebo at Texans – It's possible Skattebo escapes the coach's doghouse and bounces back after being held without a touch last week. However, it's more likely the Giants backfield remains a three-man committee with Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary also involved. The Texans aren't an ideal matchup either, having permitted the fifth-fewest rushing yards and 10th-fewest fantasy points to RBs this season.  

  • Tyler Allgeier vs. Broncos – Even with Jeremiyah Love missing another game, it's difficult for fantasy managers to trust Allgeier after he split work with Bam Knight last week. Touches were divided fairly evenly; 19-17 and the snaps weren't far off either at 56%-46%. Allgeier is just a TD-or-bust RB3.  

Michael Wilson, WR, Cardinals

vs. Broncos

Wilson's production has boggled the mind following Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade to Houston. After producing as a fantasy WR1 last season when Harrison was out of the lineup and posting 11-89-1 and 7-95-0 in the two weeks before Harrison was dealt, expectations were sky-high. 

Sadly, Wilson's targets have dropped to just seven per game and the results have been incredibly disappointing, with stat lines of 4-30-0 and 4-32-0, respectively.

The matchup doesn't get any easier this week against the Broncos. Denver is the eighth toughest opponent for fantasy receivers so far this year.

Other WRs to sit:

  • Xavier Worthy at Seahawks – Worthy has put up at least 70 yards in back-to-back games, but Seattle's defense won't make life easy on him. The Seahawks are 31st in fantasy points allowed to wideouts. 

  • Tre Tucker vs. Rams – Tucker is coming off a huge fantasy performance in an easy matchup with the Bills, but let's not forget his boom-or-bust nature. He's been held under 45 yards with no touchdowns in four of his five outings this year. Now, he battles the Rams, who have only let one receiver op 50 yards against them. This isn't a spot to take a swing on Tucker. 

  • Keenan Allen at Vikings – Things are about to get ugly in Indianapolis. The Colts are no match for a Brian Flores defense fresh off a bye. Minnesota has also kept every receiver it has faced over the last four games to 67 yards or less, with just one touchdown to wideouts during that span. 

Jake Ferguson, TE, Cowboys

at Eagles

Ferguson remains a TD-or-bust low-end fantasy TE2, whose only upside exists when injuries occur in his receiving corps. After his touchdown eruption in Week 2 and Week 3, Ferguson has been held under 20 yards in three consecutive weeks. 

The 27-year-old hasn't reached the end zone against the Eagles since 2023, so I'm not looking in his direction for a spot start this week. 

Other TEs to sit:

  • Juwan Johnson vs. Steelers (Paris) – Johnson followed up his 16-yard outing in Week 5 with zeros across the board in Week 6. That makes him impossible to trust in your lineup. With first-round receiver Jordyn Tyson expected to return after the Saints' Week 8 bye, it's time to find a fantasy replacement for Johnson.  

  • Harold Fannin Jr. at Titans – Fannin has been limited to just one catch in each of the past two weeks. Meanwhile, the Titans have held every tight end they've encountered this year to 34 yards or less. That's not exactly a recipe for fantasy success.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers's next touchdown pass will move him to third all time
item.description: As Aaron Rodgers prepares to become the first quarterback in NFL history to play in four different countries, he's on the verge of taking over third place on the all-time touchdown pass list.
item.content:encoded:
As Aaron Rodgers prepares to become the first quarterback in NFL history to play in four different countries, he's on the verge of taking over third place on the all-time touchdown pass list.

Via NBC Sports research, Rodgers needs only one more to break a tie with Hall of Famer Peyton Manning for No. 3. Rodgers and Manning are currently tied at 539.

Rodgers likely will be stuck at No. 3, given his plan to retire after the season. He needs 32 (when I taped the attached video my math skills had me thinking it was 22) to catch Hall of Famer Drew Brees with 571. Future Hall of Famer Tom Brady holds the all-time record at 649.

In six games this season, Rodgers has 12 touchdown passes and five interceptions. For his career, his 539 touchdown passes are offset by 128 interceptions, which translates to a touchdown-to-interception ratio of 4.21.

More importantly, the Steelers are trying to win their third game in a row after starting 2-2. A victory in Paris would put them at 5-2 and, possibly, all alone in first place in the AFC North (if the Browns and Ravens both lose on Sunday).

item.title: Aaron Rodgers, Steelers QBs coordinate suits, flat caps before game in France
item.description: The Steelers are also deploying a new uniform combination for the NFL Week 7 matchup outside of Paris.
item.content:encoded:
The PittsburghSteelers quarterbacks wanted to look dapper for the first NFL game in France.

Starter Aaron Rodgers, position coach Tom Arth and backups Drew Allar, Will Howard and Mason Rudolph arrived to Stade de France outside of Paris wearing suits, ties and flat caps ahead of their NFL Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

"By order of the Peaky Blinders," the team wrote in captioning its post about the coordinated outfits. It's a reference to the BBC show Peaky Blinders, which follows a fictional organized crime group in Birmingham, England, during World War I. The drama ran for six seasons from 2013 to 2022.

Required reading: Steelers new uniforms: Pittsburgh mixes, matches for NFL game in France

By order of the Peaky Blinders pic.twitter.com/mwuwMFfooM

— Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 25, 2026

The connection to France is a little flimsy considering the show is British, but it's probably not a theme worth overthinking.

The suits and caps aren't the only fashion statement the Steelers are making in this game. The team will also deploy a new uniform combination.

They'll wear black Color Rush pants along with their traditional white jerseys. It's the first-ever use of that combo.

item.title: Peyton Manning reportedly has no interest in Colts' vacant GM position
item.description: The Pro Football Hall of Famer was immediately floated as a potential replacement for Chris Ballard after Ballard was fired.
item.content:encoded:
It looks like we can rule out the possibility of Peyton Manning becoming the Indianapolis Colts' new general manager.

ESPN reported Sunday morning that the team "have not approached Manning about their vacant GM job, nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position." The Colts became the first NFL team to change general managers in 2026 when they fired Chris Ballard on Monday after a home loss to the Tennessee Titans.

The idea of the former Colts QB re-joining the organization was first publicly floated by former ESPN anchor Dan Patrick on his radio show immediately after Ballard was fired.

"And I had a source last hour, once this news broke with Chris Ballard, saying that he believes the Irsay [family] will reach out to Peyton Manning about being a GM, maybe the entry point of also having part ownership," Patrick said.

"I know that Peyton and family are happy in Colorado, he has a son who's playing high school football there. But is this enough potential to be an owner of the Colts? Is that enough to kind of lure him back to the NFL?"

The Colts dropped to 2-4 after the loss to the Titans and in the statement announcing Ballard's firing, team CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon said that the team's standard was "to compete for championships."

Ballard became the team's general manager ahead of the 2017 season. During his tenure, the Colts never won the AFC South and made two playoff appearances. The franchise faces a potential decision at quarterback given Daniel Jones' play as he returns from the Achilles injury he suffered in 2025 and the structure of his contract. And the Colts also don't have a first-round pick in the loaded 2027 NFL Draft after trading it to the New York Jets as part of a midseason trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year.

A move into the front office by a retired franchise icon is not without recent precedent. Longtime Atlanta Falcons QB Matt Ryan is in his first season as the team's president of football after working as an analyst for CBS' NFL coverage.

But Manning taking a similar job with the Colts would be an abrupt shift from his current post-playing career. Manning is still an omnipresent corporate pitchman during Sunday commercial breaks and regularly hosts the Manningcast alternate Monday Night Football broadcast with his brother Eli.

If the two-time Super Bowl champion ever wants to work for an NFL team, he'll have no shortage of suitors. But it clearly doesn't seem that a reunion with the Colts is in the immediate offing.

item.title: 5 things to watch as Jets face Dolphins in Week 7 of 2026 NFL season
item.description: Here are the main storylines as the Jets face the Dolphins in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets came up short in New England, dropping to 2-4 on the season and essentially making this weekend's game another must-win affair. 

They'll be favored at home, with Malik Willis and the winless Miami Dolphins coming to town.

Here are the main storylines to watch as the Jets aim for their first AFC East win under Aaron Glenn…

Miami's best chance for a win?

The Dolphins' season is off to a terrible start after they lost their first five games, and also lost offensive linchpin De'Von Achane to a season-ending injury.

However, they've faced some tough opposition and competed well at times. They should be motivated as they will view this game as their best shot at getting a win.

For the third time in four games, the Jets are facing an opponent that has had longer than seven days to prepare for them, and the Dolphins will no doubt have been doing some soul-searching and specific game-planning during their bye week, which could make them dangerous.

For the Jets, situational football will be under the microscope as they must do better on third and fourth down and in end-of-half situations. New York has been outscored 100-6 in the last two minutes of the first half during Glenn's tenure.

Is D'Angelo Ponds' role set to increase?

The Jets rookie has seen some playing time in recent weeks, and finished the Patriots game in a full-time slot cornerback role after Jarvis Brownlee was apparently benched following some communication breakdowns.

While it's encouraging that the coaching staff's faith in Ponds has increased, he hasn't exactly settled into his role yet, as he had two costly penalties against the Bears and gave up a long catch and a touchdown in New England.

Will Zach Sieler terrorize the Jets once again?

The Dolphins' defensive lineman has developed from being a rotational player into one of Miami's defensive leaders over the past several years, and he always seems to be at his best when facing New York.  

Sieler has played 12 times against the Jets, racking up nine sacks. Miami has a 10-2 record in those games, and he'll be eager to improve on that this Sunday. Otherwise, he could be a trade candidate in the weeks ahead.

Jacob Rodriguez vs. David Bailey

Two of the top contenders for the NFL's Defensive Rookie of the Year award will be facing off.

Bailey is off to a productive start with 31 tackles, five sacks, and three forced fumbles. However, as we've seen in recent weeks, he can be inconsistent and has made mistakes at times.

On the other hand, Rodriguez has been a model of consistency. He has racked up an impressive 57 tackles in five games, with an interception. He's had at least eight tackles in every game apart from the Chiefs game, in which he had three tackles for loss.

Can Omar Cooper Jr. build on his breakout game?

Bailey and his fellow first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq each had a recent breakout game, with Bailey recording three sacks against Cleveland and Sadiq posting a 100-yard game in Detroit. However, neither player has been able to build on that with a big performance since then.

Could Cooper, the Jets' other first-round pick, fare differently in the game after his own breakout? Cooper made his return from IR last Sunday and stepped up with six catches for 103 yards and a touchdown.

It would be nice for the Jets to get more consistency from their rookie class, and that could begin with another good game from Cooper on Sunday.

item.title: 5 things to watch as Giants face Texans in Week 7 of 2026 NFL season
item.description: Here are the main storylines to watch as the Giants face the Texans in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants were in a great position at 3-1 with four seemingly winnable games coming up. 

However, after a tie with the Commanders and a loss to the Saints, they find themselves on the verge of losing their grip on the NFC East if they lose again in Houston on Sunday.

Here are the main storylines to watch as the Giants face the Texans in Week 7…

A tough test against the resurgent Texans

A couple of weeks ago, Giants fans might have been looking ahead to this game as a potentially easy win. The Texans had just dropped to 0-4, losing to a Cowboys team that the Giants beat earlier in the year.

Things have turned around for the Texans since then, though, and they're now hoping for a third straight win that would put them right back in the mix in the AFC South.

Houston blew out the Titans by 23 to get back on track, then outdueled the Jaguars, 34-31, in an exciting shootout in London to improve to 2-4. This is now looking like one of New York's toughest games of the season so far.

J.J. McCarthy makes his first start

The recent trade acquisition has been named the starter for Sunday following a remarkable performance against the Saints last weekend.

McCarthy replaced the ineffective Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter with the Giants trailing the Saints, 34-10. By the end of the game, he had tied the all-time franchise record for passing yards in a quarter and had the Giants on the brink of an incredible comeback.

While the comeback bid ultimately fell short, it was enough to earn McCarthy his shot at starting in Houston. He was 6-4 as a starter last season, and will be eager to get off to a winning start as New York's new QB1.

Can the Giants run the ball on the Texans?

The Texans' resurgence has been credited in large part to head coach DeMeco Ryans taking on a more hands-on role with the defense, but they already had one of the best run defenses in the NFL.

Heading into the London game, they were No. 1 against the run and hadn't allowed any player to rush for 40 yards against them all year. While they actually gave up a season-high 106 yards on Sunday, they have held all of their other opponents to under 90 yards.

New York's own running game appears to be in flux as Cam Skattebo was benched for the second half of Sunday's game after reportedly complaining about a lack of touches, implying that he was being punished for a costly fumble in Washington. Veteran Najee Harris was released after complaining about a lack of touches.

Look for McCarthy to try to contribute to the running game on designed runs and scrambles.

Can Jaylin Noel continue his breakout?

Houston's best known weapon in the passing game is Nico Collins, the two-time Pro Bowler with three 1,000-yard seasons to his name. However, a new star could be emerging.

Previously considered to be mostly a return specialist, the athletic Noel had the biggest game of his career in London as he caught four passes for 107 yards and a touchdown.

Noel showcased where he's been developing his skill set with some impressive route running and good hands in Sunday's game, so he will look for more of the same against New York's banged-up secondary.

Is C.J. Stroud making the leap?

The former second overall pick hasn't had a bad start to his career, but has never really been considered to be playing up to his full potential. While he's posted a winning record as a starter in each of his three seasons, with a 4,000-yard passing season and one Pro Bowl under his belt, Stroud has arguably never looked as good as he does right now.

On course for career-best numbers in virtually every passing category, Stroud posted his third 300-yard game of the season against the Jaguars and has a sparkling quarterback rating of 116.6 over the past three weeks.

He is clearly playing with ultimate confidence right now, as evidenced by some of the tight-window throws he completed in London. It will definitely be a challenge for John Harbaugh's staff to slow Stroud down.

item.title: After Maliek Collins’ extension, Browns have 4 starters left who are set to be free agents
item.description: The Cleveland Browns roster still has 4 starters set to enter NFL free agency after Maliek Collins’ extension
item.content:encoded:
Unlike teams like the Pittsburgh Steelers, who won’t talk contract extensions during the season, which led to the trade of CB Joey Porter Jr., Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry is more than happy to get deals done whenever they might work out. Before the 2026 NFL season started, Berry and the Browns locked up CB Denzel Ward and S Grant Delpit with extensions.

Saturday night, before Week 7’s matchup with the Tennessee Titans, Cleveland extended veteran DT Maliek Collins to a big-money deal, adding another midseason extension to Berry’s resume.

Months before the season started, we listed seven probable starters who were set to hit free agency after the season. Since then, OL Teven Jenkins not only didn’t start but hasn’t played a game and is now on injured reserve. With Delpit and Collins getting extensions, that leaves just four starters on the final years of their contract:

  • QB Deshaun Watson
  • DE Isaiah McGuire
  • S Ronnie Hickman
  • P Corey Bojorquez

There have been rumblings of Watson being in line for an extension, which could be a part of a drastically changed 2027 quarterback plan.

McGuire has started all six games this season, with Myles Garrett traded away and Alex Wright out for the season with an injury, contributing three sacks, five tackles for loss, and four quarterback hits. Hickman continues to start opposite Delpit, but rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren could be in line for his position heading into next season.

Bojorquez’s contract is likely to wait until after the season.

Of the four remaining, a McGuire extension might be at a higher cost than many expect, while a Watson extension would send versions of shockwaves through Browns fans and the NFL as a whole. Hickman and Bojorquez are the most likely to hit NFL free agency in 2027.

item.title: Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets: Three Reasons Why
item.description: J-E-S-T JEST! JEST! JEST!
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins return to the playing field this week to face one of their biggest rivals: the New Yorks Jets.  For the first time this season, the Dolphins will face a team that doesn’t have a winning record or even a .500 record.  The Jets are a scrappy but bad team, just like the Dolphins.  They will have their own set of challenges for the boys in aqua and orange, so let’s get to it.

3 REASONS FOR HOPE

REINFORCEMENTS MAY BE ON THE WAY

The Dolphins got one of their key contributors back against the Bengals in week 5 in defensive tackle Kenneth Grant, though he only played 18 snaps.  He will likely be ramped up in this contest.  But the Dolphins may also be getting back their top receiver in Caleb Douglas as well as rookie safety Kyle Louis.  Both players are practicing and may return to face the Jets.  Douglas began the season as the go-to WR for Malik Willis but left in week 2 with an ankle injury.  Even if he doesn’t get a ton of stats, his presence will force the Jets’ defense to play differently to account for him.  He may be on a pitch count, but it will help the offense regardless.  Louis is a bit of a different evaluation as he only played 3 snaps on the season before going on IR.  He is also switching from being a college LB to an NFL safety.  The Dolphins safety group is playing decent right now with fellow rookie Michael Taaffe and sophomore Dante Trader Jr. being the primary safety duo.  But Louis will fill the role as a big nickel and has the athleticism and coverage skills to perhaps limit damage from the tight end position that seems to plague the Dolphins.

THE RUN GAME SHOULD CONTINUE DRIVING THE ENGINE

Ollie Gordon II is now leading the charge for the Dolphins run game.  With NFL’s NextGenStats, OG2 is tied with the league’s leading rusher Kenneth Walker III for 2nd in efficiency.  The efficiency stat measures how north/south a runner gets.  OG2 barrels downhill quickly and runs with power.  Right now, he is averaging 5 YPC, which is tied for 6th best.  The Dolphins as a team are averaging 4.9 YPC, which is 5th best. The Dolphins also added rookie Kaytron Allen from Washington via the waiver wire. He is listed at 5’11”, 217 lbs. and profiles as another downhill, north/south, power rusher.  He was acquired just before the Cincinnati game but has had 2 full weeks to get into the system.  He will likely get some game action when also considering Jaylen Wright aggravated an injury against the Bengals.  Even if he’s active, Wright may have limited touches.  The Dolphins can lean on the two bruisers to power the run game and keep the chains moving regardless.  The Jets are towards the bottom end of the league in rushing yards allowed, ranking 25th with 738 yards allowed.  They are also middle of the pack in YPC allowed, ranking 19th with 4.4 YPC allowed.  The Jets also haven’t faced a running threat at QB like Malik Willis.  I’ve mentioned in other posts and comments several ways for the passing game to help Willis get into a rhythm and build confidence.  But another way for the offense to stay in rhythm is for the QB to pick up some yards with his legs.  This is a matchup that favors the Dolphins.

THE DEFENSE CAN MAKE A STAND

It often takes some time for a new defense to gel and start playing up to the expectation.  It could take even longer with a defense with so much inexperience.  Statistically, the Dolphins aren’t as bad as their record suggests.  They are 21st in yards per play allowed.  They are 16th in passing yards per game allowed. They are 16th in rushing yards per game allowed.  They are 8th in YPC allowed.  Of course, they have that pesky completion percentage allowed issue.  But as we’ve seen in the 2 most recent games, the offenses are content to throw short for completions rather than try to push the ball downfield.  Given the Jets’ personnel – TE heavy – they will probably stick to the same gameplan.  Standout WR Garrett Wilson leads the team in targets, but his yards per reception is 11.9, which is indicative of heavier slot usage.  However, they don’t have a combination of elite offensive talent and/or an elite QB.  Geno Smith is playing better than expected and could present a problem.  However, the Dolphins secondary is playing better than expected also.  The 2 outside CBs are doing well in press coverage and Chris Johnson is improving in the slot.  Miami’s edge group is heating up.  Both Robinson and Uche are excelling in generating pressure when going 1-on-1.  Despite not having the sack numbers, Chop is one of the best in the league at generating pressure and generating it fast.  The Jets are not a dominant offense.  They are lower than Miami in yards per play.  Their passing game, while better than Miami’s (everyone’s passing game is better except Tennessee), they still do not average more than 200 yards per game, ranked 23rd at 196.2.  They aren’t a dominant rushing team either, ranking 23rd in total yards (567) and 26th in YPC (3.6).  This plays right into Miami’s top ranked YPC allowed (3.7) so I would not expect the Jets to have a great day rushing.  Altogether, the Dolphins defense has a chance to get some stops and give the offense a chance to get the ball back.

3 REASONS FOR CONCERN

THE JETS PASS DEFENSE      

Even without the passing game issues for the Dolphins, the Jets present a problem for opposing passing attacks.  The Jets overall allow only 4.8 yards per play, which is tied for 5th best.  They allow 4.2 YPC on run defense, so it is shaky.  But the passing defense is stout, allowing 185 yards per game, 4th best in the league.  They have faced 3 teams in the top 10 in passing yards per game.  Each was held well below their season averages.  They are especially good at that in their building.  In 2 homes games thus far, they’ve held Green Bay, who averages 269.3 passing yards per game to a measly 136 passing yards.  They held the Browns, who average 173.5 passing yards per game to 102 passing yards.  Green Bay pulled out a win in OT, but the Jets got a win over the Browns.  The Jets are 9th in CP allowed at 61.5%.  Not only that, but the Jets can dial up the pressure also.  The Jets are 7th in sack percentage at 8.1%.  They are 10th in pressure percentage at 24.3%.  They are also 5th in blitz percentage at 36.0%.  Former Packer Kingsley Enagbare is tied for 7th in pass rush win rate at 27% and rookie David Bailey is tied for 6th in the league with 5.0 sacks.  A stout pass defense with a high blitz rate is bad news for Miami’s struggling passing game.  The good news for the Dolphins’ offense is the Jets have allowed 130+ yards rushing in 3 of the last 4 games and none of those teams average more per carry than Miami.  The Dolphins can likely do damage on the ground, but I would not expect this to be the “breakthrough” game for Malik Willis.  In fact, the passing game may be uglier than ever this game.

CURSE OF METLIFE STADIUM

MetLife Stadium has seemingly been cursed for players to be injured.  It’s a tough road environment, despite the MetLife Takeover.  But the field surface is always a major concern.  Just because the Dolphins aren’t contending this season doesn’t mean potential injuries aren’t bad.  Just like with any team, the Dolphins can ill afford major injuries.  Maybe not for the win column aspect, but with the developmental arc of most of this team.  Maybe I’m overly concerned about this, but that stadium and field scare me in this regard.  Praying for good health for the players over anything else.

ON THE ROAD AGAIN

The Dolphins will have their 4th road game in 6 contests.  That in and of itself is tough.  Add in the struggling offense, hit-or-miss defense, and the divisional aspect, and this will be a rough go for the Dolphins.  The Jets are 2-4 and just lost a division game against the Pats.  The Pats will go on the road to face a tough Chicago team at night.  The Jets are going to want to stay in this divisional race for as long as they can.  Even at 2-4, they are dangerous.  They have only lost one game by more than 1 score and that was by only 11 points.  They are not a pushover team.  And then there’s the win-loss aspect.  The Dolphins have enjoyed a decade of success against the Jets in Joe Robbie Hard Rock Stadium.  But at Met Life, the teams have nearly alternated wins every season for the last 12 contests beginning in 2014.  The bad news to go along with that is if that trend continues, it will be Miami’s turn to lose.  Given the circumstances…

I SAID WHAT I SAID

Divisional matchups mean chaos.  During the Tom Brady era of the New England Patriots, the Dolphins went into New England and won a total of 3 times. The most notable is the 2008 Wildcat Game.  Miami had its fair share of notable wins over the Pats in Miami (Michael Thomas game, Miami Miracle). But 2008 was the last time the Dolphins would see victory in New England.  Until 2019, when the “tanking” Dolphins went into Gillette Stadium in week 17 and stole a win from a Brady led team that finished 12-4 and was still fighting for playoff positioning.  Had the Pats won that game against a 4-win Dolphins team, they finish 13-3, get a first-round bye, don’t immediately face a feisty Derrick Henry led Titans team and if they make it, would host the Chiefs, who went on to win the championship, at home.  So don’t think the Pats didn’t care about that game!  Yet, the Dolphins got that win.  The Jets are arguably the better team right now.  They have a QB that is playing better right now.  But that doesn’t mean the Dolphins are automatically out.  They played well against a better Vikings team on the road and hung tight against a good Bengals team.  Miami has a clear advantage in both rushing offense and defense.  This could easily be a loss, but it just as easily be the first win for the Dolphins.  In this division, you just never know.

item.title: Steelers new uniforms: Pittsburgh debuts new look for NFL game in France
item.description: The Steelers have worn black pants in the past, but almost all of those instances have come at home with black Color Rush jerseys.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are debuting a new twist on one of their classic uniforms. 

It isn’t strictly a new design that they’re turning to for their NFL Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, Oct. 25.

Rather, first-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team is patching together features of existing uniform combos to create something new for what will be the first NFL regular-season game in France at Stade de France outside Paris. 

Required reading: DK Metcalf has prime chance to spark Steelers offense in Paris vs. Saints

What’s new about the Steelers’ uniforms? 

Typically, the Steelers wear yellow pants for their road games. Against the Saints, however, they’ll be wearing their black Color Rush pants along with their traditional white road jerseys.

Tomorrow’s kit 🥶@_Dwfootball11 | @nickherbig_pic.twitter.com/8QwaRvK720

— Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) October 24, 2026

The Steelers have deployed black pants in alternate uniform combinations of the past. Typically, however, they’ve worn them at home with black Color Rush jerseys. Their most recent appearance was Dec. 15 of last season, when they defeated the Miami Dolphins at Acrisure Stadium on "Monday Night Football."

This kit makes more conspicuous use of contrast to create a new look for a road contest. So far, it seems to have been well received. 

"Now seeing it together, it's unique for us to wear," tight end Darnell Washington told the team website. "It's a little bit different, but I like it.

"We are playing in a different environment, so it's cool to mix and match. It's a look good, feel good, play good feeling.

"Me personally, I don't think much about what I am wearing. I just wear the same thing and go out and play."

The Steelers traveled to France late in the week. The Saints, meanwhile, have been on the ground since early Monday. They flew across the Atlantic Ocean following their NFL Week 6 against the New York Giants. 

It’s the second international game for Pittsburgh in as many years. Last season, they defeated the Minnesota Vikings in the first NFL game in Ireland. 

They wore their traditional home uniform for that one. This time, however, it appears the uniform managers wanted to try something different. 

"It's cool, and we're going to have to see it on game day," linebacker Nick Herbig told the team’s website. "But I'm a fan. I think it looks good.

"It's a little change-up, something different. Like they say, when in Rome, but we're going to be in Paris, so let's do it."

item.title: The Colts could trade Jonathan Taylor, and/or others, before the deadline
item.description: Seahawks, Broncos, Vikings, Packers are linked to Taylor.
item.content:encoded:
With the Colts turning the page at the top of the front office — and possibly, in time, at the top of the coaching staff — the possibility of trading veteran players is on the table.

But with the deadline still 16 days away, and with most of three full weekends left to be played, it's still too early to sell off contracts.

Via the Batman-and-Joker turned Batman-and-Robin of ESPNFL, the plan is to see whether the Colts can improve their 2-4 record in the coming three games against the Vikings, Jaguars, and Cowboys before deciding whether to trade away certain players.

The biggest name of the bunch belongs to running back Jonathan Taylor. Per the carefully (but also a little clunkily) worded report: "The Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Vikings are among the teams that have, or are expected to, pondered the possibility of a trade for the star running back, according to sources."

That feels like an effort by the Colts to maximize the market, in an effort to maximize the return. The more teams that are at the table, the more the Colts will get for their biggest star.

The Colts gave Taylor a new contract in the offseason, a two-year, $44 million extension. A trade would result in a 2027 cap charge of $10 million, and it would shift the final two years of his current deal to his next team, at a compensation package of $16.02 million for 2027 and $17.98 million in 2028. The deal also has $1 million in incentives attached to each of the final two seasons.

The Colts don't have a first-round draft pick in 2027, thanks to the Sauce Gardner trade. Surely, they'd want at least that much for Taylor, especially after giving him a $15 million signing bonus when Taylor signed his extension.

Of the teams that were listed, the Vikings, Broncos, and Seahawks make the most sense. Each is a contender with an offense that would benefit from the presence of an elite tailback. The Packers, who are getting Josh Jacobs back today, make the least sense; adding them to the list seems to be nothing more than an effort to get the Vikings to give up a little more in an effort to ensure he won't land with a viable division rival.

Other potential trade candidates mentioned by the report include veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (who could go back to the 49ers, who traded him to the Colts), guard Quenton Nelson (who's in the last year of his deal), and defensive tackle Grover Stewart.

Whatever the Colts do, or don't do, at the trade deadline will impact the deck of cards the next G.M. has. Without knowing who the next G.M. will be, it's impossible to know whether that person would prefer to have Taylor moving forward or whatever the Colts can get for him.

Regardless — and this is true for any team thinking about trading players before the deadline — the remaining weeks will be a factor. Some teams won't be ready to make their moves until Week 9 has ended; in some cases, the final decision hinges on winning or losing in the last game before the window closes.

item.title: Will Byron Young get a sack (or two) against Raiders?
item.description: Will the Los Angeles Rams be able to lean on Byron Young and their defense against the Las Vegas Raiders?
item.content:encoded:
Will Byron Young have a massive game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday? Young has been a good player for the Los Angeles Rams, he’s been great at times, but this year the defense isn’t generating enough sacks. That includes Young.

The team is getting pressure, but the defense and Young need to finish with sacks. Pressures aren’t enough against the best quarterbacks in the league.

It’s been a theme for 2026 that this Rams team is good some important areas. They are generating yards, they are holding teams out of the endzone, there are positive in this 2-4 season.

But the Rams aren’t scoring enough points to win, and the defense isn’t making the key stops at the end of games. The special teams are a mess.

So, can the Rams get right on Sunday? Young having a big game would help.

3 Bold Predictions in the Los Angeles Rams’ Showdown With Kirk Cousins and the Raiders (athlonsports)

“Los Angeles Rams fans will make the drive up I-15 this weekend for a team that badly needs a road

win. The Rams are 2-4 after an 18-16 loss to Arizona, they’ve lost Davante Adams for six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury, and Kirk Cousins and the Las Vegas Raiders are waiting at Allegiant Stadium. Sean McVay has said the Rams’ depth can handle it for now.

Byron Young sacks Kirk Cousins twice

Byron Young has 29 pressures, sixth among 115 edge defenders, and his 22 hurries lead the position, according to PFF. He has only four sacks, though, and the Rams have just eight as a

team despite one of the league’s best pressure rates. They turn pressure into sacks just under 10% of the time, second-worst in the NFL, and we called the pressure-to-sack gap the first fix before Cousins this week.“

Top Rams News: Previews and predictions for Rams at Raiders on Sunday in Las Vegas for Week 7 (therams.com)

“Here’s a collection of analysts’ predictions and previews for Rams-Raiders:

Nine of the 11 ESPN experts chose the Rams to come out on top on Sunday against the Raiders. Picks for every game can be viewed here.

Three of the five NFL.com analysts picked the Rams to beat the Raiders. All their picks are here.

Six of the eight Sports Illustrated staffers picked the Rams to win against the Raiders. All of their Week 7 predictions can be seen here.“

Lawrence McCutcheon Dies at 76 After Parkinson’s Diagnosis, Rams Legend Made 5 Pro Bowls (bleacherreport)

“Former Los Angeles Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon, a five-time Pro Bowler who amassed four 1,000-yard seasons, has died at the age of 76 after a lengthy battle with Parkinson’s disease.

The McCutcheon family revealed news of his passing via a statement, which the Rams shared on Friday.“

Rams’ defensive front shuffling ahead of Raiders matchup (ocregister)

“But the Rams will have to rely on players like Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison to play bigger roles this week and into the future.

“Definitely felt terrible,” Davis said of when he learned about Turner and Ford’s injuries. “But also just wanted to get in the mindset just step up for my guys, for real.”

For Davis, whose role has grown with the Rams over the past two-plus years, he will try to keep things to his usual process, not changing the way he studies or prepares even with more snaps coming his way.

“Just focus on our core four and then having the right mindset to go out there and execute, play throughout the full down and fall in love with the process of it,” Davis said with a tablet playing practice tape on his lap. “Just get to it.”

Rams have a prime chance to get the run game in rhythm vs. Raiders (ramblinfan)

“Not only does McVay need to get Williams in rhythm, Blake Corum finally showed signs of life as well last week. His nine carries for 42 yards made for his best rushing performance since Week 2 versus the Giants. For the Rams’ run game to really get going, both Williams and Corum need to be effective. 

Williams only carried 10 times against Arizona, for 50 yards. He has 393 rushing yards on the season, on 4.9 yards per carry, plus 217 yards receiving. The Rams don’t need to force-feed Williams on the ground if Corum is also productive, but they should look to get him touches one way or another. His 13 touches in Week 6 were his fewest of the season.“ 

3 Critical Matchups the Rams Must Win vs. Raiders to Avoid Falling to 2-5 (si.com)

“The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. This will be a must-win game for the Rams as they look to avoid a 2-5 start. While the Raiders may have been seen as a guaranteed win in recent years, that’s not the case this season. The Raiders have played well and nothing is guaranteed with this Rams team. Let’s dive into the three biggest matchups to watch. 

RT Warren McClendon Jr. vs. EDGE Maxx Crosby

For the most part, Warren McClendon stepped in well for an injured Rob Havenstein. So much so that when Havenstein was healthy at the end of the year, the Rams simply stayed with McClendon and then didn’t draft a replacement when they could have in the first round. However, there were signs that McClendon may not be what the Rams needed when he allowed 11 pressures over three playoff games, including five against the Carolina Panthers and four against the Seattle Seahawks.“

3 causes for concern for Raiders Week 7 vs Rams (sports.yahoo)

“3. Raiders banged up running back room

Speaking of running back duos. The Raiders are on the other end of the spectrum in terms of their running attack this season. They were already 31st in the league in terms of yards per attempt (3.0). Much of that has been due to Ashton Jeanty not being quite himself while fighting through ankle and foot injuries. Now backup Mike Washington Jr is also hurt. The rookie back showed up on the injury report this week with foot and back injuries, causing him to miss Friday’s practice and be Questionable for the game. With Jeanty averaging under 2.5 yards per carry the past couple weeks, the Raiders really need to Washington as the change-up.“

Vegas, baby, Vegas! Why the Rams’ season could go bust in Sin City (nypost)

“Because what began as a season filled with Super Bowl aspirations has become a five-alarm fire, and the team that dreamed of playing for a Lombardi Trophy in its own stadium might need a miracle just to escape the NFC West basement.

After consecutive home losses, including Sunday’s humiliating 18-16 defeat to the previously 1-4 Arizona Cardinals, the Rams (2-4) head to Allegiant Stadium for a Week 7 showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3).“

Rams’ 5 keys to victory vs. Raiders on Sunday (ramswire)

“Do not let the Raiders isolate Quentin Lake or Jaylen McCollough on Bowers, and bait Las Vegas into throwing the out route. They always look for it; setting it up will give a defender inside leverage to stop those attacks, and Cousins throws it blindly.

Regardless, if the Rams stop Bowers, their offense should do enough to win.“

Rams need a new kind of offense to overcome injuries and mend inconsistency (ramblinfan)

“New injuries have lengthened the growing list of benched veterans. Kicker Blake Grupe and nose tackle Poona Ford are now out for the season. Entering Week 7, LA has eight players from the 53-man roster on injured reserve. But injuries continue to occur. Right now, the casualty count has reached nearly a dozen.


For a team trying to turn the corner, injuries create unwanted uncertainty. The Rams’ struggling run defense will be strained to its limits without Ford and Landman. They will face the Las Vegas Raiders also without defensive tackle Kobie Turner, one of the recent IR additions.

The offense could be without its top two receivers. LA has already targeted Nacua and Adams more than 100 times this season; their joint absence would force the offense to transform.“

One thing his brothers are kinda knuckleheads themselves.
